<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Show a product's version, its latest release and the next version its branch asks for.

```text
Reads the `versioning:` block of anchors.yaml and shows, for one product:

  sources    the version each source file holds (they must agree)
  released   the latest release: the highest tag of the product reachable from HEAD
  branch     the strategy the branch resolves to, and the rule that decided it
  next       the version that strategy computes, and why

A `Version:` footer on a commit since the release forces the next version. `--json` prints the
same as data, with the commits since the release already classified: it is the context a
project's own script receives to decide a version.

`anchors version bump` writes a version into every source, and `anchors version apply` brings
the version the branch asks for into the repository as the product's `apply:` says.
```

## Usage

```bash
anchors version [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--branch` |  | the branch whose strategy decides (default: the current branch) |
| `--json` |  | print the state as JSON |
| `--product` |  | the product of `versioning:` (needed when there are several) |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## Subcommands

### `anchors version apply`

Bring the version the branch asks for into the repository, as the product's apply: says.

```text
apply: release_pr (the default) opens, or updates, the pull request anchors/release/<product> →
the branch, carrying the version in every source, the release's block in every changelog output
and the intents it consumed. Merging it is the release.

apply: commit confirms the sources already hold the version the branch asks for: a bump made by
hand, with anchors version bump.

apply: build writes the version into the sources of the workspace, commits nothing, and prints
version= and tag= (also into $GITHUB_OUTPUT): the tag alone records it.
```

#### Usage

```bash
anchors version apply
```

### `anchors version bump`

Write the next version into every source of the product.

```text
With no argument, writes the version the branch's strategy computes. A part of the
scheme (`major`, `minor`, `patch`, a pattern's group) raises the version the sources hold; an
exact version is written as given. Whatever decides it, the version must be readable, above the
one the sources hold and not below the latest release. Only the version's bytes change in each
file.
```

#### Usage

```bash
anchors version bump [part|version]
```

## Versions, changelog, pull requests and pipeline — family

Commands of the same family — what tells each apart:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **`anchors version`** | Show a product's version, its latest release and the next version its branch asks for |
| [`anchors changelog`](/docs/cli/commands/changelog/) | Build the technical changelog from the commits, release by release |
| [`anchors commit-msg`](/docs/cli/commands/commit-msg/) | Confront the commit message with the format the changelog will read |
| [`anchors pr-body`](/docs/cli/commands/pr-body/) | Write the lines linking this work's cards, in the platform's syntax |
| [`anchors backfill-labels`](/docs/cli/commands/backfill-labels/) | Write into open issues the links the new version began to mark |
| [`anchors report`](/docs/cli/commands/report/) | Generate reports in docs/ by perspective (cuts of what Anchors measures) |
| [`anchors branch`](/docs/cli/commands/branch/) | Confront merges and commits with the project's branch flow (`branch_flow:`) |
| [`anchors pipeline`](/docs/cli/commands/pipeline/) | Ask whether a stage of the pipeline may run, and record that it passed (`pipeline:`) |
